# The `unblock-prs` skill in this repository

What the skill (`libs/pr-merge-queue/claude-plugin/skills/unblock-prs/`,
linked into `.claude/skills/`) leaves to the repository. `CLAUDE.md` holds
too, above all "Session rules" and "Commits and pull requests": a fix is
amended onto the branch's one commit, and `pnpm run fmt` runs on it.

## Commands

Run every command through the root script, never `node_modules/.bin`:
`pnpm run pr-report -- --format json`, `pnpm run claim-pr -- <n> --by <c>`,
`pnpm run push-fixed-pr -- …`, `pnpm run report-unowned-prs`, and
`pnpm run rebuild-pnpm-update -- …`. The scripts run the package from its
sources, so they work before anything is built.

## The dependency update

`chore/pnpm-update` is generated by `pnpm-update.yml`, and listed under
`generatedBranches` in `unblock-prs.json`. A conflict on it is resolved by
`pnpm run rebuild-pnpm-update -- <number> --by <claimant>`, which starts the
workflow; its force-push at the end is the hand-back. Refused for
want of `actions: write`, say so, release the claim and leave it.

## Reproducing a check

**The check name is the command.** `style-check (X)` and `code-check (X)` both
run `pnpm run X` at the repository root, so `code-check (check:knip)`
reproduces as `pnpm run check:knip`. Five checks do not follow that rule:

| Check                        | What to run                                                    |
| :--------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `test-node-versions (<ver>)` | `pnpm run ws:build` then `pnpm run ws:check:test` on that Node |
| `verify-published`           | `pnpm run verify:npm-packages:published`                       |
| `backup-repository-settings` | `pnpm run repo-settings:backup`, then look for a dirty tree    |
| `Validate PR title`          | The PR title is not Conventional Commits — `PATCH /pulls/{n}`  |
| `Validate commit count`      | The branch is more than one commit — squash it, see below      |

`code-check (check:root)` also needs `actionlint` and `shellcheck` on `PATH`,
at the versions `code-check.yml` pins; `check:root:actionlint` names them and
where to get them when they are not there.

`Validate PR title` is required because a squash merge takes the PR title as
the commit title (`squash_merge_commit_title: PR_TITLE`), so the fix is the
title itself, not the branch. It checks Conventional Commits and English;
`skip-ci` in a title means nothing to any workflow, which reads the label
instead.

`Validate commit count` is the same rule about the other half of the squash
commit: the branch's subjects become its body, so the branch is one commit.
Squash with `git reset --soft "$(git merge-base HEAD origin/main)" && git commit`
in the worktree. If the message is not obvious from the PR title and body,
stop and ask.

- `code-check (*)`, `style-check (ws:doc)`, `style-check (ws:check:ext)` and
  `style-check (ws:gen)` run `pnpm run ws:build` first in CI. Do the same
  locally or they fail for the wrong reason.
- Every job ends with `z:assert-repo-is-clean`. So `fix:fmt:full`, `ws:doc`,
  `fix:codemod:full`, `ws:fix:lint` and `ws:gen` fail by _changing_ files.
- `code-check` and `node-version-compatibility` jobs gate on
  `z:check-should-run:code-checks`, and `style-check` jobs on
  `z:check-should-run:style-checks`; both diff against `origin/main`. A job
  that reports green having skipped its steps is expected on a docs-only
  branch (or, for every workflow, an `experimental/`-only one), not a problem
  to chase.

`grep ELIFECYCLE` in a job log names the command that actually failed.

## Decisions left to a person

The comment that leaves one is in Japanese. **`check:root:licenses` failing is
always a decision**, usually on the dependency update: an update brought in a
license `tools/configs/license-policy.mts` does not let through. An exception
added to turn it green is the check switched off; say which package, which
version, and from which license to which.
